backfillDays.title: Days of mail to fetch on the first sync

secretShape.description: Use an app-specific password when your mail provider offers one. Do not enter your normal mail password unless your provider explicitly says it supports password-based IMAP access.

setupInstructions.title: Check which password your mail provider requires
setupInstructions.description: For Gmail, Outlook.com, or Microsoft 365, prefer Gezel's dedicated connector so you can authorize through the provider's website. Use generic IMAP for other providers or when your provider specifically supports an app password.
steps: Gmail: use the Gmail connector when possible. Otherwise, with 2-Step Verification enabled, create a 16-digit App Password in your Google Account security settings.
iCloud Mail: at account.apple.com, open Sign-In and Security, then App-Specific Passwords, and generate one for Gezel.
Yahoo Mail: open Yahoo Account Security, then External connections, and create an app password for Gezel.
Outlook.com or Microsoft 365: use Gezel's Outlook.com or Microsoft 365 connector instead of generic IMAP whenever possible.
For another provider, check its IMAP documentation before entering a password. Use a dedicated app password if it offers one.

notes: A window, not a mirror. The first sync of each folder fetches the messages received in the last backfillDays days (default 90), newest first, a batch at a time; after that every new message arrives. Read/unread and other flag changes on messages already synced are not picked up, and messages later moved or deleted stay in the corpus. If the server renumbers a folder (a UIDVALIDITY change), the window is synced again without duplicating anything. Sending needs SMTP settings and is deny-by-default: only recipients on the binding's allowed recipients/domains lists can be sent to, and night shift defers sends to the outbox for daytime approval. Saving a draft appends the message to the mailbox's Drafts folder for you to review and send yourself; it never transmits, so it needs no allowlist.
